Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T17:55:35Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy reflects errors recorded on frontend-proxy's own spans. Two paths contribute. (1) The dominant path: frontend-proxy's 'ingress' spans return HTTP 504 because POST /api/checkout is aborted by frontend-proxy's own 15 s upstream timeout (access log '504 UT response_timeout', 15000-15001 ms, upstream 'frontend'), while frontend's POST /api/checkout and checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder ran ~89 s; inside that request checkout's 'orders publish' span (88.87 s) fails with 'circuit breaker is open' / 'kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker', and checkout's logs show metadata fetch and dial i/o timeouts to the Kafka Service IP 100.71.78.255:9092. The Kafka brokers show their own controller-side pathology: the active QuorumController retries CreateTopics for 'orders'/'__consumer_offsets' (TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS) and rejects the broker directory assignment with StaleBrokerEpochException ('Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10'), with 'STALE_BROKER_EPOCH. Retrying.' from broker/controller id 1. Both kafka pods log controller/broker id 1 activity, consistent with the Deployment's 2 replicas presenting a duplicate broker identity and never completing replica assignment, so produce requests block until timeout. (2) A later, secondary contributor: ad-554b849958-4chjq's container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 18:13:16Z with a 450Mi limit; from ~18:14:35 to ~18:22:35 frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and GET /api/data spans error at ~0.6 spans/s and frontend-proxy began returning 500 on GET /api/data, raising the ingress error rate after the alert had already started. frontend-proxy itself is healthy (ready, 0 restarts): its 504s are its upstream timeout firing on slow dependencies, not a proxy fault. No node pressure and no restarts of kafka/frontend-proxy pods were observed.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's span metrics contain exactly two operations with STATUS_CODE_ERROR series in the window: span_name 'ingress' (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and 'router frontend egress' (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT); status_code values present are STATUS_CODE_ERROR, STATUS_CODE_OK and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

frontend-proxy 'ingress' ERROR span rate was ~0.24-0.48 spans/s from the first sample at 17:56:35 through 18:13:35, rose to 0.81-1.02 spans/s at 18:15:35-18:21:35, and fell back to ~0.31-0.39 spans/s at 18:23:35-18:26:35; the sibling 'router frontend egress' ERROR rate was 0 until 18:14:35, peaked 0.62 spans/s at 18:16:35, and returned to 0 at 18:23:35.

No pre-alert baseline exists for these span metrics: the 1-minute query returns its first sample at 17:56:35 (source_start_at 17:56:35) and a 5-minute-step query started at 14:00 returns its first sample only at 18:00:00.

In trace f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1 the visible parent-child chain is: load-generator POST 504 (15.0039 s) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' error=true http.status_code=504 (15.0019 s) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' error="true" http.status_code=0 (15.0017 s) -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' http.status_code=200 lasting 89.085 s -> frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 89.083 s -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 89.082 s (rpc.grpc.status_code 0) -> checkout 'orders publish' 88.872 s with otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open'.

frontend-proxy's access log shows the alerting errors as its own upstream timeouts: 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout' with durations 15000-15001 ms against upstream 'frontend' 100.96.4.175:8080; 68 such lines fell in 18:10:30-18:13:00.

In 18:16:00-18:22:00 frontend-proxy logged 223 lines containing ' 504 ' (sampled lines are all POST /api/checkout 504 UT response_timeout), and in 18:15:00-18:22:00 it logged 280 lines containing ' 500 ' on 'GET /api/data' (upstream 2-3 ms, response body 21 bytes).

frontend's own error spans ('GET', 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds') each ran at ~0.47-0.63 spans/s from 18:14:35 to 18:22:35 and were 0 outside that interval.

checkout's logs contain repeated 'client/metadata got error from broker -1 while fetching metadata: read tcp 100.96.1.134:58594->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout', 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout', 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open', 'Failed to write message: kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker' and 'kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open'.

The Kubernetes Service 'kafka' in otel-demo is a ClusterIP on 100.71.78.255 with plaintext port 9092 (and controller 9093), which is exactly the address checkout timed out dialing; both kafka pods (kafka-ff7884766-skk8d at 100.96.2.21, kafka-ff7884766-xclnk at 100.96.4.61) are listed as ready endpoints of that Service.

Kafka broker logs show a persistent controller-side assignment/epoch failure: '[QuorumController id=1] CreateTopics result(s): CreatableTopic(name='orders' ...): TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS' repeating, 'assignReplicasToDirs: event failed with StaleBrokerEpochException ... Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' repeating about every 10 s, and '[ControllerApis nodeId=1] Unexpected error handling request ... AssignReplicasToDirsRequestData(brokerId=1, brokerEpoch=10, ...)' between 17:58:23 and 17:59:55.

The other kafka pod's log shows the same pathology continuing: '[QuorumController id=1] CreateTopics ... __consumer_offsets ... TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS' at roughly 10 log lines per second from at least 18:09:15 through 18:24:11, and '[AssignmentsManager id=1] handleResponse: 50 assignments failed; global error: Response-level error: STALE_BROKER_EPOCH. Retrying.'
Deployment otel-demo/kafka has spec.replicas 2, and both kafka pods are owned by ReplicaSet/kafka-ff7884766, are Running/ready with restartCount 0 and started at 17:43:37-17:43:38Z.

Pod ad-554b849958-4chjq container 'ad' has restartCount 1 and lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 and finishedAt 2026-11-16T18:13:16Z (container restarted 18:13:16Z); the ad container's memory limit is 450Mi (request 225Mi).

ad was serving normally immediately before the OOM: at 18:11:40-18:11:42 the ad service's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in 42 ms and 3 ms, with frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and GET /api/data returning http.status_code 200.

ad's log contained only 418 lines across 18:12:00-18:26:00, and the newest 40 lines shown are normal request handling ('Targeted ad request received for [...]', 'no baggage found in context') from 18:23:52 to 18:24:09; no error/panic/OOM lines matched in the window.
At 18:20:35 the frontend-proxy 'ingress' error rate was 1.2407 spans/s of STATUS_CODE_ERROR alongside 7.3593 spans/s of STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no STATUS_CODE_OK series was returned for this span_name).

The deepest supported cause of the 504 path is the Kafka cluster in otel-demo/kafka: the brokers cannot complete replica assignment, so the 'orders' topic has no servable partition leader for clients ('Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker'), producing on orders blocks ~89 s in checkout, checkout's PlaceOrder exceeds frontend-proxy's 15 s timeout, and frontend-proxy records 504. The most likely mechanism is that the Deployment's 2 replicas present a duplicate broker node identity (both pods log controller/broker id 1 and brokerEpoch 10 while the controller expects epoch 17), which would explain both the epoch churn and the intermittent dial timeouts to the Service IP; this duplicate-identity mechanism is not verified because the pods' env/startup configuration could not be read.

The ad container OOMKill at 18:13:16Z is a second, independent contributor to the same alert metric rather than its trigger: it plausibly explains frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and GET /api/data error spans at ~0.6 spans/s from 18:14:35 to 18:22:35 and frontend-proxy's new '500' responses on GET /api/data, which together raised the ingress error rate from ~0.3-0.48 to ~0.8-1.02 spans/s after the alert had already started at 17:55:35. Direct evidence of ad being unreachable during 18:14-18:22 was not obtained (trace queries for the ad service in that interval returned no data).

frontend-proxy being the origin of the errors (proxy failure, restart or misconfiguration) is rejected: its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-59tsm is Running/ready with restartCount 0, the failing responses are logged as its own '504 UT response_timeout' with upstream 'frontend', and the same requests complete upstream after ~89 s (http.status_code 200 in the frontend span), so the proxy is reporting a slow dependency rather than failing itself.

Node-level resource pressure as the cause of the Kafka timeouts is not supported by the current cluster state: all 5 nodes report Ready=True, MemoryPressure=False and DiskPressure=False, and the kafka pods have restartCount 0.

Other services visible in the same trace showed no failure: payment 'charge' 337 us, cart GetCart 492 us, shipping /get-quote 1.859 ms, quote POST /getquote 343 us, product-catalog GetProduct 106 us, currency Convert 522-719 us, email send_email 3.1 ms - all with grpc status 0 or http 200 - so this is not a cluster-wide latency event.

accounting's 'orders receive' ERROR span rate was 0 in every returned sample of the window, i.e. that consumer-side series shows no observed error signal in these metrics, even though the producer side (checkout) is failing.

Treat otel-demo/kafka as the primary fix: make broker identity unique and stable (one broker, or a StatefulSet/unique KAFKA_NODE_ID per pod with a shared cluster id) so AssignReplicasToDirs stops failing with StaleBrokerEpochException and the 'orders' topic regains an online leader; verify via metadata-quorum/metadata logs that no further 'Expected broker epoch X, but got broker epoch Y' lines appear.

Separately address the ad OOMKill: raise the ad container's 450Mi memory limit or investigate ad memory growth, and confirm frontend degrades gracefully instead of returning 500 on /api/data when the ad service is unavailable.

Decouple the request path from the Kafka produce: have checkout publish asynchronously or with a short client timeout so a stalled broker cannot hold PlaceOrder for ~89 s and let frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout turn it into 504s.

gaps: No pre-alert baseline exists for frontend-proxy span metrics: the earliest returned sample is 17:56:35 (essentially the alert start 17:55:35), so whether the 'ingress' error rate of ~0.3-0.48 spans/s was already abnormal before 17:55:35 cannot be established.

Kafka pod logs are only available from ~17:58:23 (kafka-ff7884766-xclnk), and the other pod's log stream hit the 4 MiB read limit at 18:09:22, so the broker's startup identity configuration (KAFKA_NODE_ID, cluster id) and the exact onset of the epoch churn are unverified.

The kafka Deployment's container env/startup configuration could not be read (kubernetes_jq_query on deployments returned INVALID_PARAMS), so the duplicate-node-id mechanism behind the STALE_BROKER_EPOCH loop remains a hypothesis rather than an observed fact.

Prometheus has no alerting rules loaded: list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for type=alert both returned no data, so the alert expression, threshold and evaluation history are unknown.

Kubernetes events returned no non-Normal events inside the window, and no Evicted/OOMKilled event for the ad pod was observed (events may have expired); the ad OOM is established from the pod's lastState, not from an event.
The previous (OOMKilled) ad container instance's logs were unavailable ('previous terminated container not found'), so what drove ad's memory over 450Mi is unknown.
No ad-service traces were returned for 18:14-18:20, so ad's serving gap in that interval is inferred from the OOM timestamp plus frontend/proxy errors rather than directly observed.
frontend container logs returned no data for 18:13-18:24, so frontend's own log-level explanation of its GetAds/GET /api/data errors is unknown.
The change_history integration is not available, so no configuration or image change preceding the incident could be checked.
next_steps: Inspect the kafka Deployment/StatefulSet configuration (KAFKA_NODE_ID, KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID, controller quorum settings, replica count) and broker metadata logs to confirm or refute duplicate broker identity.
Check topic description / metadata-quorum for the 'orders' topic to confirm partitions have no online leader while the epoch loop is active.
Review the ad container's memory profile and set a limit/probe combination that keeps the ad service available; verify how frontend handles GetAds failures (HTTP 500 today).
Review frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout against checkout's real latency budget and add an alert that distinguishes 'upstream slow' (UT) from genuine proxy errors.
